LESSON: VOLUME OF SOLIDS

Grade: Grade 9
Subject: MATHEMATICS
Strand: Measurements 3.1 Area (8 lessons) • Area of a pentagon and a hexagon • Surface a
Topic 3.2: Volume of Solids

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! Today we learn about Volume of Solids. Read the explanation, study the examples, do the practice, then try the revision quiz.

Big question: How do we determine the volume of different solids?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. calculate the volume of a triangular, rectangular, and square-based pyramid

SECTION 3: LEARN STEP BY STEP

• Today’s maths focus is Volume of Solids.

• Start with objects you can touch or draw — stones, sticks, bottle tops, or drawings in your book.

• Say the steps aloud as you work so you do not skip a stage.

• Check your answer with a second method or by estimating.

SECTION 4: EXAMPLES

Example 1: At the market, count 10 mangoes and put them in 2 groups of 5.

Example 2: In class, count the desks in your row and write the number in figures and in words.

Example 3: If you have 7 shillings and receive 5 more, you have 12 shillings.

SECTION 5: TRY THIS

1. Solve three short problems about Volume of Solids using drawings.
2. Explain one solution to a partner in your own words.
3. Make up one new word problem set in your county or school.

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (PRACTICE & REVISION)

1. Write five practice questions and solve them in your book.
2. Show your working clearly — not only the final answer.
3. Teach a younger learner one idea from this lesson with bottle tops or drawings.

SECTION 7: CLASS ACTIVITY IDEAS

1. Identify and discuss the model of a prism. Using the relevant formulas, determine the volume of a prism.
2. Identify and work out the volume of models of a pyramid. Cut the pyramid into two parts to get a frustum and a small pyramid and determine the volume of the frustum using the relevant formula.
3. Critical thinking and Problem-solving: learner identifies and works out the volume of a frustum from a pyramid.
4. Creativity and Imagination: as the learner identifies, discusses, and works out the volume of solids. Values:
5. Responsibility: learner takes care of the models of pyramids, cones, and spheres.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. How do we determine the volume of different solids?
2. How do we use the volume of solids in real- life situations?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Use objects or drawings when a sum feels hard.
2. Check every answer.
3. Volume of Solids is used in real Kenyan life — market, school, and home.

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open the Answers tab only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original learner lesson from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
